svg.title: PHP as a trade-off between one label operation and end-to-end QoS visibility
svg.desc: Two parallel paths compared. With PHP enabled, the penultimate hop pops the transport label, the egress PE receives a bare IP packet, saves a lookup, and loses the EXP bits, so MPLS-based queueing cannot be applied on the last segment and traceroute shows an address that is not the egress interface. With PHP disabled and an explicit null configured, the penultimate hop hands over label 0, the egress PE keeps EXP for queue scheduling and traceroute shows the real last address, at the cost of one extra label operation and a possible carrier policy that forbids the change. A bottom band states the three questions to ask the carrier before committing to end-to-end QoS.
svg.text: PHP is not a switch; it is a trade between one lookup and one QoS guarantee
The same physical path behaves differently for voice depending on this single decision
PHP ENABLED · implicit null (label 3)
PE (egress)
receives plain IP
pops label
+ saves one label operation and one lookup on the egress
+ the last core hop does less work
− EXP is gone: the egress cannot queue on MPLS class
− traceroute shows an address that is not the egress interface
PHP DISABLED · explicit null (label 0)
PE (egress)
receives label 0 + EXP
swap to 0
+ the egress PE keeps EXP and can schedule the last segment
+ traceroute reveals the real last hop
− one extra label operation and lookup per packet
− many carriers will not let a customer change this

text.tspan: Ask the carrier these three things, in writing, before you promise end-to-end QoS:

svg.text: 1. Is the last hop implicit null or explicit null, and is it the same for every class of service (and after a maintenance window)?
2. How does my DSCP map to the carrier's EXP or TC values, and is the mapping preserved across the core?
3. If EXP is discarded at the last hop, what is the carrier's guarantee for the final segment — a queue, a policer, or nothing?
Verification you can run yourself: send a marked flow and read the egress counters per class. If the class counter does not move, the marking never reached the queue —
and the answer is in this figure, not in the bandwidth graph everyone was staring at.
